items.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013
items.q: I had real problems with the publisher, who was the son of the original publisher, old man Maher, who had his quirks but I was able to get along with him

ctx.x: What about race, racial issues in jazz now?

Now — I think it’s pretty good now from what I can see. We went through some ups and downs. I was with DownBeat during a relatively interesting time as in the Chinese saying “may you live in interesting times.” There was a lot going on. You know there was a phenomenon which is very understandable and logical and was bound to happen sooner or later. In spite of the fact that jazz was one area where there were really good relations between the races, there was a residue of built-up and, you know, resentment among…

there was — Newport in New York had, in the beginning, in their earlier years, they had some side events, panel discussions and stuff. And I was invited — this was just around the time when I was leaving DownBeat because I had real problems with the publisher, who was the son of the original publisher, old man Maher, who had his quirks but I was able to get along with him and you knew where he was coming from. His son was really somebody who came in without having any experience with or knowledge of jazz other…
